prompt_text: Who is the best personal injury lawyer in Pleasanton California?
answer_verbatim:
There isn’t a single objectively “best” personal injury lawyer for everyone — the right lawyer depends on your type of injury, how serious it is, whether fault is disputed, and your preferences (trial lawyer vs settlement negotiator, communication style, fee structure). I can’t browse the web from here, so I won’t give names I can’t verify, but I can help you find and evaluate the best local attorney for your case.

Where to look
- State Bar of California lawyer search (verify license and discipline history)
- Review sites: Avvo, Martindale-Hubbell, Super Lawyers, Google and Yelp (look for patterns, not single reviews)
- Local bar association referrals (Alameda County Bar Association)
- Recommendations from people you trust or other attorneys (e.g., a family lawyer referring a personal injury specialist)

What to prioritize
- Experience with your type of case (car accident, slip and fall, dog bite, medical malpractice, etc.)
- Track record of settlements and trials — trial experience matters if the insurer won’t settle
- Contingency-fee agreement (common in PI cases) and clarity about expenses
- Good communication: prompt, clear answers and a team to handle routine matters
- Local courtroom experience and knowledge of local insurers/judges

Questions to ask in a free consult
1. How many cases like mine have you handled? Outcomes?
2. Do you try cases or mostly settle?
3. Who will handle day‑to‑day work — you or associates/paralegals?
4. What is your contingency fee and how are costs handled if we don’t recover?
5. Estimated timeline and likely settlement range based on past results?
6. Any conflicts or reasons you couldn’t take my case?

Typical fee/expense notes
- Contingency fees commonly 33%–40% (may vary if case goes to trial)
- You may be responsible for advanced costs (investigators, medical records) — confirm whether firm advances them
- If there’s no recovery many firms waive fees/costs — verify in writing

Red flags
- Guarantees of specific dollar outcomes
- Pressure to sign immediately
- Vague answers about trial experience or fees

If you want, tell me:
- Type of injury, date/location, whether you’ve seen a doctor, and whether the other party/insurance is known — I can then suggest specific search terms, a short list of qualifications to filter by, and a script/email you can use to contact firms. If you’d like, I can also draft a message to send to multiple firms to request a consultation.
